facts.label: What address should I use for Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: Use 7600 East La Palma Avenue, Anaheim, CA 92807. The park stretches more than a mile, so use the official map to select the closest numbered parking, playground, shelter, lake, or trail connection.

facts.label: What hours is Yorba Regional Park open?
facts.value: The park opens daily at 7 a.m. and closes at 9 p.m. in spring and summer or 6 p.m. in fall and winter. The office and bike or paddleboat rental counter close earlier.

facts.label: How much is parking at Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: Vehicle entry is $3 Monday-Friday and $5 Saturday-Sunday. Some holidays and events have higher rates. Park in the numbered area nearest your selected playground, picnic shelter, lake, or trail.

facts.label: Are there playgrounds at Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: Yes. Playgrounds and restrooms are distributed throughout the long park. Check the official map before arriving so families can choose the closest entrance and parking area.

facts.label: Can I reserve a picnic shelter at Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: Yes. The park has seven reservable group shelters, more than 400 picnic tables, many permanent shade structures, and about 200 barbecues. Unreserved facilities may be first come, first served under posted rules.

facts.label: Can I bike from Yorba Regional Park to the Santa Ana River Trail?
facts.value: Yes. Paved bicycle routes meander through the park and connect directly with the Santa Ana River Trail. Walking, multi-use, fitness, and equestrian routes are also mapped, with different permitted uses.

facts.label: Are dogs allowed at Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: Yes, dogs are permitted on leash. Owners must follow OC Parks rules and keep dogs out of any signed restricted activity or facility area.

facts.label: Can I rent a bike or paddleboat at Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: Bike and paddleboat rentals operate on their own schedule. The last bike rental goes out one hour before sunset and the last boat rental two hours before sunset on operating days; check the vendor's current hours before visiting.

facts.label: Where are the restrooms at Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: Restrooms are located throughout the park rather than at one central building. Because Yorba Regional Park is more than a mile long, check the official map and park in the numbered area closest to the restroom, playground, shelter, or lake you plan to use.

facts.label: Can I fish or swim in the lakes at Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: Fishing is allowed, but California requires a state fishing license for visitors age 16 and older. Swimming and wading are prohibited, and visitors may not launch personal watercraft; model sailboats are limited to the designated lake.

facts.label: What can be closed or seasonal at Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: Park closing time changes seasonally: 9 p.m. during spring and summer daylight-saving months and 6 p.m. in fall and winter. Bike and paddleboat rentals keep separate operating days and stop rentals before sunset; storms, flooding, maintenance, events, or fire restrictions can also affect trails, lakes, shelters, roads, and barbecues. Check the OC Parks alerts page before a feature-specific trip.

facts.label: Where can I find shade or shelter at Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: Many of the park's 400-plus picnic tables have permanent shade structures, and seven group shelters can be reserved. Trees also shade portions of the stream and lake corridor, while ballfields, playgrounds, volleyball areas, open lawns, fishing edges, and long trail sections can be exposed. The park office has limited weekday hours, and picnic roofs are not severe-weather shelters; during lightning, flooding, or high wind, use an open substantial building or vehicle.

facts.label: Can visitors swim or use a splash pad at Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: No. Yorba Regional Park has no listed splash pad, and OC Parks prohibits swimming or wading in its lakes and connecting streams. Fishing, designated model sailboats, and concession-operated paddleboats are different activities and do not permit entering the water. Keep children and pets out of the lakes and use a separately listed aquatic facility for swimming or splash play.

facts.label: Can I take a bus to Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: OCTA Route 38 runs along La Palma Avenue toward Anaheim Hills and Yorba Linda. The park is long, so confirm the stop closest to your intended lake, playground, shelter, or trail access and expect a final walk; use OCTA's current trip planner because service times and stop patterns can change.

facts.label: What are the main landmarks in Yorba Regional Park?
facts.value: Four connected lakes and streams form the park's visual spine and support fishing, model boats, and seasonal paddleboat rentals. The park stretches for more than a mile beside the Santa Ana River, with playgrounds, restrooms, picnic tables, and seven reservable group shelters distributed along its length. Choose a lake, shelter, playground, or trail connection before parking rather than treating the first entrance as the whole park.

The recreation center, pool buildings, concessions, and amphitheater spaces open only for their own programs or events. Use the shelters for ordinary sun or light rain, but move to an open substantial building or enclosed vehicle for lightning, strong wind, or dangerous heat.

facts.label: What are the walking surfaces and routes at Pearson Park?

facts.label: What can I do at Great Park besides sports?

facts.value: OC Parks identifies concrete pathways throughout the developed park, supporting walking, jogging, wheelchairs, strollers, and bicycles. The separate 123-acre wilderness area has more natural conditions.

facts.label: Can I reserve a picnic shelter at Mason Regional Park?
facts.value: Yes. A large-group shelter can be reserved, and additional family picnic areas, tables, restrooms, lawns, and shade trees are available. Organized uses must follow OC Parks reservation and vendor rules.

facts.label: Are dogs allowed at Mason Regional Park?
facts.value: Yes, dogs are permitted on leash. Keep them restrained and out of any signed restricted facility, sports, habitat, or event area.

facts.label: Are there restrooms at Mason Regional Park?
facts.value: Yes. Restrooms are listed with developed picnic and recreation areas. Use the park map to identify the facility closest to your playground, shelter, lake, or trail route.

facts.label: Is Mason Regional Park accessible for wheelchairs?
facts.value: The developed park has concrete pathways, accessible parking and curb ramps, and picnic tables with wheelchair overhangs. The separate 123-acre natural area has less predictable terrain, so use the developed lake, playground, and picnic zones when a paved route is important.

facts.label: Can I swim or wade in the lake at Mason Regional Park?
facts.value: No. Swimming and wading are prohibited, and visitors may not launch personal watercraft. The lake is used for viewing and organized model sail boating; follow all posted shoreline barriers and event controls.

facts.label: Is there shade at Mason Regional Park?
facts.value: Yes. OC Parks describes rows of mature shade trees throughout the developed park, especially around lawns and picnic areas. Playgrounds, trails, and the lake edge can still be exposed, so select a shelter or tree-lined picnic zone when guaranteed shade matters.

facts.label: Can visitors swim or use a splash pad at William R. Mason Regional Park?
facts.value: No. Mason Regional Park has no listed splash pad, and OC Parks explicitly prohibits swimming or wading in its lake or creek. Watercraft are also prohibited. Treat the 9.2-acre lake as scenery and wildlife habitat, keep children and pets out of the water, and choose a separately operated Orange County aquatic facility for managed swimming or water play.

facts.label: Can I take OC Bus to William R. Mason Regional Park?
facts.value: OC Bus serves the Irvine and UC Irvine area, but OC Parks does not identify one guaranteed park-front route. Use OCTA's current trip planner with 18712 University Drive and verify the stop, final crossing, and return service before leaving; the lake, playgrounds, shelters, amphitheater, and sports fields are spread through the property. Do not rely on an older route number because OCTA schedules change quarterly.

facts.label: What are the main landmarks in William R. Mason Regional Park?
facts.value: The developed park centers on a 9-acre lake used for scenery and model boats, with nearby picnic areas, playgrounds, paths, and an amphitheater. A separate 123-acre wilderness and natural area occupies another part of the property. Choose the lake, amphitheater, reservable shelter, playground, or wilderness area before parking because this 339-acre park is much larger than a single lawn or lakefront stop.

Route directly to the zoo, playground, trail, garden, or sports facility when that is your priority.

facts.label: How much is Balboa Park parking in 2026?
facts.value: Paid parking remains active through December 31, 2026. Road meters are $2.50 per hour, and lots range from $5-$16 depending on residency, location, and duration. Lower Inspiration Point gives nonresidents three free hours; verified San Diego residents receive free or discounted lot parking.

facts.label: Is there a free shuttle inside Balboa Park?
facts.value: Yes. The free accessible tram normally runs daily from 8 a.m.-8 p.m. every 10-15 minutes from Inspiration Point, serving Plaza de Panama, the Organ Pavilion, and Pan American Plaza. It may pause for holidays or special events.

facts.label: Is Balboa Park accessible?
facts.value: Accessible parking is free without a time limit for vehicles displaying a valid disabled-person plate or placard, and all free trams have accessible ramps. Route accessibility still varies among historic buildings, gardens, canyon trails, and individual attractions.

facts.label: Where are playgrounds in Balboa Park?
facts.value: Family play areas are distributed across the park, including Pepper Grove and Sixth Avenue zones. Because Balboa Park is very large, use the official facilities map and navigate to the exact playground rather than the park name.

facts.label: Where can dogs go off leash at Balboa Park?
facts.value: Balboa Park has three designated off-leash dog parks. Dogs must remain leashed elsewhere and follow posted restrictions around gardens, playgrounds, buildings, athletic facilities, and protected canyon habitat.

facts.label: Is Balboa Park free?
facts.value: Outdoor park entry, many gardens, public architecture, playgrounds, trails, and picnic landscapes are free. Museums, the zoo, some gardens, performances, attractions, events, food, and current parking charge separately.

facts.label: Will Balboa Park parking become free again?
facts.value: The City says the current paid-parking program ends January 1, 2027. Until then, use the live City parking page because rates, resident verification, passes, lot access, holidays, and event closures can change.

facts.label: Where can families find restrooms in Balboa Park?
facts.value: Restrooms are destination-specific rather than centralized. Pepper Grove has on-site restrooms beside its playground and picnic grounds; Pine Grove and several West Mesa picnic areas also have nearby facilities. Museums and attractions keep their own hours, so use the park map for the closest public facility.

facts.label: Where is a good family picnic area in Balboa Park?
facts.value: Pepper Grove is a practical family base with 15 picnic tables, shade trees, a large playground, grass, and on-site restrooms. Pine Grove is another shaded option on the West Mesa. Larger organized gatherings may require a reservation or permit.

facts.label: Where can I find shade in Balboa Park?
facts.value: Shade varies widely across the 1,200-acre park. Pepper Grove and Pine Grove are specifically tree-shaded family areas, while Tram Central at Inspiration Point provides benches and shade. Open plazas, lawns, and canyon trails can be exposed, so choose the destination rather than assuming continuous shade.

facts.label: What are the walking surfaces and slopes in Balboa Park?
facts.value: The central cultural district uses hard-surface promenades, plazas, sidewalks, ramps, and bridges between museums, gardens, theatres, and the Prado. Canyon and hiking routes are very different, with compacted dirt, decomposed granite, rocks, roots, erosion, stairs, and substantial grades. Even developed destinations are widely separated across the 1,200-acre park; use the facilities map and the ADA-ramp-equipped free tram for the cultural core, and choose a named trail only after checking its current surface and elevation.

facts.label: Is there a splash pad or swimming pool in Balboa Park?
facts.value: Balboa Park does not have a general free splash pad. Bud Kearns Memorial Pool is a separately operated City aquatic facility in the Morley Field area, with its own admission, swim schedule, closures, and program rules. The Lily Pond and the park's decorative fountains are not water-play areas, so visitors should not enter them; check the pool's current schedule before making it the purpose of a trip.

facts.label: Where should I start to see Balboa Park's major landmarks?
facts.value: Start at Cabrillo Bridge on the west side and walk east through the historic El Prado cultural district. That route leads toward the California Tower, Spanish Colonial Revival facades, Plaza de Panama, El Cid statue, Botanical Building and Lily Pond, and several museum courtyards. Balboa Park is too large for one landmark pin, so use this central corridor for architecture and art, then route separately to the Moreton Bay Fig, Japanese Friendship Garden, or attractions beyond the Zoo side.

facts.label: Where should I go in Mission Bay Park?

facts.label: Is parking free at Mission Bay Park?
facts.value: Most public lots are free, but gates and overnight restrictions vary by location. Mission Point's lots are free and close at 10 p.m.; Fiesta Island allows parking around the island during its 4 a.m.-10 p.m. hours.

facts.label: Are there restrooms at Mission Bay Park?

facts.label: What are the paths and surfaces like at Mission Bay Park?

facts.label: Are there playgrounds at Mission Bay Park?

facts.label: Where can dogs go at Mission Bay Park?
facts.value: Fiesta Island is leash-optional except in fenced nesting and youth-camp areas. Elsewhere in Mission Bay, leashed dogs are allowed only outside seasonal daytime restrictions: before 9 a.m. and after 4 p.m. in winter or after 6 p.m. in summer.

facts.label: Can I picnic at Mission Bay Park?
facts.value: Casual picnicking is generally practical in designated lawn or table areas. Reserved shelters, permitted events, and sports use can control a specific space.

facts.label: How do I check Mission Bay water closures?

facts.label: How much shade is available at Mission Bay Park?

facts.label: Where can visitors swim at Mission Bay Park?

Choose a named bay destination and swim only inside posted swimming areas; vessels may not use designated swim zones. Lifeguard coverage and restrooms vary by location and season, and visitors should check San Diego County's current beach-and-bay closure and water-quality status before entering.

facts.label: Which part of Mission Bay Park should I visit?

facts.label: What address should I use for Waterfront Park?
facts.value: Use 1600 Pacific Highway, San Diego, CA 92101. The north side contains active recreation and dog facilities; the south side contains the children's play zone and picnic areas.

facts.label: What hours is San Diego Waterfront Park open?
facts.value: The park is open daily from 6 a.m.-10 p.m. The office, information booth, reflecting pools, fountain jets, equipment loans, snack bar, and events use shorter or separate hours.

facts.label: Are the Waterfront Park fountains working?
facts.value: The reflecting pools are currently operating daily from 9:30 a.m.-6 p.m., but the north and south fountain jets remain temporarily off for repairs as of July 31, 2026. Check the official page before traveling specifically for water play.

facts.label: Where should I park for Waterfront Park?
facts.value: Use metered street spaces or nearby paid lots; the County recommends transit. The Little Italy trolley stop and MTS bus routes 280, 290, 923, and 992 serve the area.

facts.label: Where is the playground at Waterfront Park?
facts.value: The children's play zone is on the south side near picnic areas, chess and bocce. The north recreation area has basketball, pickleball, fitness equipment, table tennis, a native garden, dog area, restroom, and information booth.

facts.label: Is there an off-leash dog area at Waterfront Park?
facts.value: Yes. The north recreation area has a designated off-leash enclosure. Dogs must remain on a leash no longer than six feet everywhere else and are not allowed in the fountains.

facts.label: Can I reserve a picnic area at Waterfront Park?
facts.value: Yes. Picnic areas near the play zone and six Civic Greens can be reserved. Groups of 100 or more, cooking, catering, alcohol, glass, amplified sound, large equipment, or performances require permits.

facts.label: Do events close Waterfront Park?
facts.value: Yes. Concerts, festivals, setup, maintenance, weather, and private reservations can close all or part of the park. Check the official closure notice and event calendar before a special trip.

facts.label: Are there restrooms at San Diego Waterfront Park?
facts.value: Yes. Public restrooms and diaper-changing space are in the park's central fountain and playground area near the County Administration Center. Rinse showers are on the outside wall of the restroom building. Event closures or maintenance can affect access even while other lawns remain open.

facts.label: Where can I find shade or weather shelter at San Diego Waterfront Park?
facts.value: Trees provide limited shade near portions of the playground, gardens, and picnic areas, but the Civic Greens, fountains, courts, dog park, and much of the waterfront lawn are exposed. Personal shade canopies are allowed on grass when placed within the park's stake restrictions. The County Administration Center is not a guaranteed public refuge, so identify a nearby open substantial building before visiting during extreme heat, lightning, heavy rain, or high wind.

facts.label: What are the walking surfaces and accessible routes at San Diego Waterfront Park?
facts.value: The downtown civic park is generally flat and developed, with broad paved plazas, sidewalks, promenade routes, and paths connecting the County Administration Center, Civic Greens, playground, fountains, restrooms, courts, dog park, and bayfront. Fountain spray can leave nearby pavement wet and slippery, while lawns, play surfacing, gardens, event fencing, and temporary stages differ from the main hard-surface route. Use the paved perimeter and marked accessible approaches during events or maintenance closures.

facts.label: Which trolley station is closest to San Diego Waterfront Park?
facts.value: Use County Center/Little Italy station on the UC San Diego Blue Line or Green Line. MTS places Waterfront Park about 0.2 miles from the station, beside the County Administration Center. Santa Fe Depot is another practical connection for the park's southern side and regional rail. Check live service and event notices because downtown festivals and waterfront celebrations can increase crowds or alter access.

facts.label: Where are the main features in San Diego Waterfront Park?
facts.value: The historic County Administration Center is the park's central landmark, with lawns and the long interactive fountain extending toward the bay. The playground and garden rooms occupy separate areas, while the northeast corner contains the active recreation zone with basketball, pickleball, fitness equipment, and an off-leash dog area. Check the fountain update before visiting because north and south basins can operate independently during maintenance.

facts.value: Use the Raspberry Road entrance and Kincaid Chalet at the west end of Raspberry Road for the main trail, stadium, and visitor hub. Other trail connections exist, so choose the trailhead shown on the official map.

facts.label: What hours is Kincaid Park open?
facts.value: Published municipal guidance lists the Raspberry Road gate from 10 a.m.-10 p.m., its parking lot until 11 p.m., and the Jodhpur gate until 9 p.m. Chalet and holiday hours are separate and seasonal, so confirm current notices.

facts.label: What trails are at Kincaid Park?
facts.value: More than 40 kilometers of routes support cross-country skiing, running, walking, and mountain biking. Trail uses and grooming vary by season; use the current ski or summer trail map rather than assuming every route allows every activity.

facts.label: Does Kincaid Park connect to the Coastal Trail?
facts.value: Yes. Kincaid provides the western connection to the Tony Knowles Coastal Trail and access toward the Anchorage Coastal Wildlife Refuge. Plan distance and return transportation before combining park and coastal routes.

facts.label: Is there parking at Kincaid Park?
facts.value: Yes. The main Raspberry Road approach has substantial parking around Kincaid Chalet and the stadium area. Ski races, tournaments, rentals, and major events can fill or redirect the closest spaces.

facts.label: Are there restrooms at Kincaid Park?
facts.value: Restrooms and visitor services are concentrated at Kincaid Chalet and developed event areas, not throughout the trail network. Chalet hours and holiday closures can affect indoor access.

facts.label: What views can I see from Kincaid Park?
facts.value: Clear conditions can reveal Cook Inlet, Mount Susitna, Denali, and the Chugach Mountains. The park also supports bird and wildlife viewing near the coastal refuge; observe animals from a safe distance.

facts.label: What should I check before using Kincaid trails?
facts.value: Check current grooming, race closures, weather, wildlife notices, gate times, and seasonal trail-use rules. Snow, freeze-thaw, darkness, and organized events can change which routes are practical or open.

facts.label: Is there an off-leash dog area at Kincaid Park?
facts.value: Kincaid has a designated Hundeplatz dog-training area at the World Cup Start Area. Use that named area for training or off-leash activity and follow posted controls; ordinary park trails have their own seasonal dog, ski-track, and wildlife rules.

facts.label: What family recreation is available at Kincaid Park?
facts.value: Kincaid includes a playground, sledding hill and amphitheater, soccer complex, disc golf, trails, and broad viewing areas in addition to competitive skiing facilities. These destinations are spread out, so use the official map rather than expecting them beside the chalet entrance.

facts.label: Do Kincaid Park's disc golf and archery facilities require planning?
facts.value: The park has an 18-hole disc golf course plus field archery and biathlon ranges. General park access is free, but organized use, range operations, tournaments, and maintenance follow partner or municipal schedules; confirm the specific facility before arriving.

facts.label: Where can I find weather shelter at Kincaid Park?
facts.value: The Kincaid Outdoor Center, commonly called the Chalet, is the park's principal indoor facility, and a picnic shelter serves the playground area connected by an asphalt path. The Chalet has posted operating, rental, and holiday schedules and should not be assumed open whenever trails are open. Forest provides wind and sun cover on many routes, but coastal overlooks, stadiums, ranges, and exposed winter trails remain vulnerable; during wildfire smoke, high wind, extreme cold, or severe weather, use a confirmed-open building or vehicle.

facts.label: Can I reserve the picnic shelter at Kincaid Park?
facts.value: Yes. The Kincaid Park picnic pavilion serves the playground area and can be reserved through Anchorage Parks and Recreation in full-day or half-day blocks. A paid reservation provides exclusive use of the shelter, tables, benches, and any listed fireplace; the Kincaid Outdoor Center is a separate reservable indoor facility. Contact the facility first for availability and current fees, especially during ski events, races, and peak summer weekends.

facts.label: Is there a swimming area or splash pad at Kincaid Park?
facts.value: Kincaid Park does not list a designated swimming area, public pool, or splash pad. Little Campbell Lake is one of the park's natural and trail-based features, while Anchorage lists its supervised swimming programs at separate municipal pools. Do not promise lake swimming based only on the map; use a listed municipal pool and confirm its current open-swim schedule when aquatics are the priority.

facts.label: Does Far North Bicentennial Park connect to city trails?

facts.label: Are there restrooms in Far North Bicentennial Park?

facts.label: Can I bring a dog to Far North Bicentennial Park?
facts.value: Dogs use many Anchorage trails, but leash, skijoring, mushing, groomed-track, and wildlife rules vary by route and season. Keep full control, protect set ski tracks, remove waste, and use the designated trail map.

facts.label: Are Far North Bicentennial Park trails accessible?
facts.value: Accessibility varies sharply by trailhead and route. Some multi-use corridors and new bridges are wider and developed, while singletrack and natural routes include roots, grades, mud, snow, and narrow sections. Confirm the exact route before relying on it.

facts.label: What should I check before using Far North Bicentennial Park trails?
facts.value: Check grooming, construction, freeze-thaw and mud conditions, daylight, and wildlife notices. Anchorage specifically warns that trails are shared with bears, moose, and coyotes and recommends making noise in bear country.

facts.label: Where can dogs be off leash in Far North Bicentennial Park?
facts.value: The North Gasline Trail is Anchorage's designated off-leash trail in this park. Dogs must be leashed while entering and leaving, licensed and vaccinated, under control and in sight, and owners must remove waste; other trails may require a leash or have seasonal restrictions.

facts.label: Which Far North Bicentennial trails are reserved for dog mushing?
facts.value: Anchorage's dog-mushing network includes dedicated routes maintained by the Alaska Sled Dog and Racing Association. Do not walk, bike, ski, or bring loose pets onto a posted mushing-only trail, because doing so can endanger visitors, dogs, and mushers.

facts.label: Can I use Far North Bicentennial Park after dark?
facts.value: Treat posted trailhead and park hours as controlling, and plan around Anchorage's rapidly changing seasonal daylight. Bring illumination for any permitted low-light outing, but do not assume every gate, lot, or groomed route remains available overnight.

facts.label: Where can visitors warm up or get out of the weather near Far North Bicentennial Park?
facts.value: The boreal forest provides summer shade but is not protection from wind, lightning, extreme cold, or falling trees. The adjacent BLM Campbell Creek Science Center offers indoor exhibits and restrooms Monday through Friday, 9 a.m.-4 p.m., except federal holidays, with its gate generally open 8 a.m.-5 p.m.; it is not an after-hours emergency shelter. Carry weather layers and return to a vehicle or open substantial building before conditions deteriorate.

facts.label: Is there a playground at Far North Bicentennial Park?
facts.value: Anchorage does not identify a conventional playground within Far North Bicentennial Park. This is a 4,000-acre urban wildland with more than 80 miles of trails for hiking, biking, skiing, dog mushing, skijoring, and wildlife viewing. For play equipment, choose one of Anchorage's neighborhood or inclusive playgrounds instead. Here, select a short mapped route, carry layers and bear-aware supplies, and keep children close around wildlife, creek crossings, winter cold, bikes, and remote trail junctions.
facts.sourceLabel: Municipality of Anchorage Parks and Recreation

facts.label: Where can I picnic at Far North Bicentennial Park?
facts.value: The clearest developed picnic option is the shelter at Abbott Loop Community Park trailhead on Elmore Road near 80th Avenue, which also provides direct access to the Far North trail network. Other major access points such as Smokejumper, Campbell Airstrip, and the Bivouac trailheads are primarily parking and trail access, not guaranteed picnic facilities. Anchorage publishes a general park and shelter rental process but does not clearly list this shelter's reservability online, so contact Parks before planning exclusive use; for a trail meal, pack out all food and waste and follow bear-aware practices.
facts.sourceLabel: Municipality of Anchorage Parks and Recreation

facts.label: Can children swim or use a splash pad at Far North Bicentennial Park?
facts.value: No developed splash pad, pool, or designated swim beach is listed in Far North Bicentennial Park. Its creeks, wetlands, and small waters are natural habitat, not supervised water-play facilities; avoid entering them and expect cold water, unstable banks, wildlife, and seasonal ice. Goose Lake Park is Anchorage's nearby developed lake-and-beach destination, but its current swimming and lifeguard status should be confirmed before visiting.

facts.label: What are the main landmarks in Far North Bicentennial Park?
facts.value: This is an urban-wilderness trail system rather than a monument or public-art park. Use the Campbell Creek Science Center area, Campbell Airstrip Road trail access, or a named trailhead as your orientation point. Campbell Creek, bridge crossings, wetlands, and the dedicated winter mushing-trail network are defining features. Never enter groomed dog-sled trails on foot, skis, or bicycle when snow-covered, because fast teams can approach quietly.

facts.label: Are there public restrooms at Delaney Park Strip?

facts.label: Is Delaney Park Strip accessible?

facts.label: Is there shade or weather shelter at Delaney Park Strip?

facts.label: Is there a splash pad or swimming at Delaney Park Strip?

facts.label: Is Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve free?

facts.label: How accessible is Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve?

facts.label: Are dogs allowed at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve?

facts.label: Is Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve good for children?

facts.value: Choose a destination-specific access point. Downtown users can begin near Morehead and Blackwell; Elmira Avenue Park, Solite Park, and C.M. Herndon Park provide useful developed stops along the Durham section.

facts.value: Use the trail according to posted daylight and park rules. Connected parks, restrooms, events, maintenance projects, and neighboring jurisdictions can use separate schedules.

facts.label: What are the paths or trails like at American Tobacco Trail?
facts.value: The Durham section is 11 miles of paved off-road former rail corridor. Users should keep speeds below 10 mph, watch for other users, and use care at street-level crossings and spurs.

facts.label: What can families do at American Tobacco Trail?
facts.value: Families can choose a short out-and-back from a park with restrooms or travel a longer section with bicycles and strollers. Teach children to keep right and stop clear of through traffic.

facts.label: Can I bring a dog to American Tobacco Trail?

facts.label: Can I picnic at American Tobacco Trail?
facts.value: Use picnic facilities at connected parks rather than stopping in the travel lane. Organized events, vendors, and group setups require permission from the relevant jurisdiction.

facts.label: What landmarks or areas should I look for at American Tobacco Trail?
facts.value: The trail links downtown Durham, neighborhoods and parks, historic rail-corridor landscapes, the Riddle Road Spur, the Chatham County line, and the larger route toward Jordan Lake.

facts.label: What closures or conditions can affect American Tobacco Trail?
facts.value: Storm damage, bridge or pavement work, street projects, vegetation management, flooding, and jurisdiction-specific maintenance can create detours. Check Durham trail notices before a long through-trip.

facts.label: Where is the best entrance for San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: Choose a trail access before navigating. Neptune Way is the western end; Foussat/Alex Road, Douglas Drive, and inland connections serve different mileage points and parking patterns.

facts.label: What hours is San Luis Rey River Trail open?
facts.value: Use during daylight hours. The trail has no lighting, and the City discourages travel after dark; construction can close individual access points.

facts.label: Where should I park for San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: Parking is available at selected access points, not continuously along the trail. The Douglas Drive lot has had construction-related restrictions, so check current notices.

facts.label: Are there restrooms at San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: Do not rely on restrooms or water along the trail. Use coastal, park, or neighborhood facilities before entering a long segment.

facts.label: Is San Luis Rey River Trail free?
facts.value: Public trail access is free. Parking and connections vary by access point.

facts.label: Is San Luis Rey River Trail good for children?
facts.value: The separated, mostly level pavement can work well for families, but distance, sun, faster bicycles, limited services, and river edges require planning.

facts.label: What accessibility details should I know at San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: The paved Class I surface supports wheelchairs and other nonmotorized users, though access ramps, construction, debris, and distance between exits vary.

facts.label: Are dogs allowed at San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: Leashed dogs are allowed for walkers and runners; leashes must be no longer than six feet, and waste must be removed.

facts.label: What amenities are at San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: Paved traffic-separated trail, river and bird views, mileage access points, benches and kiosks at selected entrances, and transit connection near the west end.

facts.label: What should I know before visiting San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: There are no lights and limited shade or services. Carry water, yield predictably, keep right, announce passes, and choose a turn-around distance before starting.

facts.label: How do I check closures or facility changes at San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: Check the linked City of Oceanside page and posted notices before a time-sensitive visit. Fields, trails, water access, restrooms, and reservable spaces can close independently.

facts.label: How much shade is available at San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: Shade is intermittent and should not be assumed along the full route. Bring sun protection and water, especially for exposed lagoon, ridge, river, or coastal sections.

facts.label: Can I picnic at San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: Use only designated tables or durable stopping areas and pack out waste. Sensitive habitat, narrow trails, and exposed overlooks are not suitable for spreading out.

facts.label: What are the paths and surfaces like at San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: Expect a mix of firm developed approaches and natural dirt, gravel, sand, roots, grades, or seasonal mud. A stroller-friendly entrance does not guarantee a stroller-friendly full route.

facts.label: Can I buy food or drinks at San Luis Rey River Trail?
facts.value: Permanent food service is not guaranteed. Bring water and snacks unless the official page or an event listing confirms an open concession.

facts.label: What weather or condition check matters before visiting San Luis Rey River Trail?

facts.value: The free lot has more than 100 marked standard and accessible spaces but regularly fills on pleasant weekends. Parking outside marked spaces is prohibited.

facts.value: The parking lot is accessible only from northbound George Washington Memorial Parkway. Cross the wide footbridge from the lot; there is no vehicle access onto the island.

facts.value: A comfort station and drinking fountains are on the south end along Woods Trail, about one-third mile from Memorial Plaza. Do not expect a restroom at the parking lot or memorial itself.

facts.label: How do I check swimming conditions at Fort Lauderdale Beach?

facts.label: Is there a splash pad on Hollywood Beach Broadwalk?
facts.value: Yes. Charnow Park at 300 Connecticut Street has a children's splash fountain, playgrounds, shaded seating, pavilions, restrooms, and restored paddleball courts. It follows its own posted operating conditions and can close for weather or maintenance even when the beach remains open.

facts.label: Are dogs allowed on Hollywood Beach?
facts.value: Dogs belong only in the city's designated Dog Beach between the Pershing and Custer Street lifeguard stands. No pass is currently required and the designated area is open sunrise to sunset. Dogs must be controlled, have a current rabies tag, and remain leashed outside Dog Beach.
facts.sourceLabel: City of Hollywood Parks, Recreation and Cultural Arts

facts.label: Can I reach Hollywood Beach without parking on the barrier island?
facts.value: The Hollywood Sun Shuttle serves the beach and Downtown Hollywood connections. The city's beach map also marks shuttle stops near parking hubs. Check the current service area, app-request rules, fare, and operating hours because those details can change.

facts.label: Can I bike or skate on Hollywood Beach Broadwalk?
facts.value: Yes. The brick-paved Broadwalk is used by pedestrians, joggers, bicycles, rollerblades, and other human-powered users. Motorized recreational devices are prohibited, while mobility devices used for disability access remain allowed. Stay in the designated path and yield to pedestrians.
facts.sourceLabel: City of Hollywood Parks, Recreation and Cultural Arts

facts.label: When are lifeguards on duty at Hollywood Beach?
facts.value: Hollywood Beach Safety operates year-round, seven days a week. Current hours are 9:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m., extended to 7:00 p.m. for holidays and special events. Swim near an open tower, check warning flags, and leave the water for thunder or lightning.

facts.label: Are there places to eat along Hollywood Beach Broadwalk?
facts.value: Yes. The city describes beachfront restaurants, bars, shopping, and rentals along the Broadwalk. Hours and prices belong to each operator, so do not rely on a particular business being open late; carry water and identify a backup before a long walk.

facts.label: What are the main landmarks on Hollywood Beach Broadwalk?
facts.value: The strongest family and culture stops are Charnow Park's water playground and pavilions, Hollywood Beach Theatre at Johnson Street, the brick Broadwalk itself, accessible beach entrances, public-art displays, and the guarded Atlantic shoreline. North Beach Park and Dog Beach are separate northern destinations.
facts.sourceLabel: City of Hollywood Parks, Recreation and Cultural Arts

facts.label: How do I check current Hollywood Beach conditions?
facts.value: Use the city's Beach Safety Conditions link and read the warning flag at the nearest lifeguard tower. Lightning, rip currents, surf, marine life, king tides, storms, or special events can change a safe route or close water access without closing the entire Broadwalk.

facts.label: What should families know before visiting Hollywood Beach Broadwalk?
facts.value: Choose the subsite first, then park near it; the Broadwalk is nearly 2.5 miles long. Charnow Park is the best dedicated play-and-splash stop, Johnson Street is the central theatre and accessible-beach hub, and lifeguard hours are shorter than park hours. places.name: Anne Kolb Nature Center

facts.label: Hours
facts.value: The nature center exhibit hall is currently open daily from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Outdoor trails, tower, programs, rentals, and gates can follow separate posted or weather-dependent schedules.

facts.label: Cost and fees
facts.value: The nature center and exhibit hall currently have no admission fee. Programs, rentals, reserved facilities, and any posted weekend or holiday gate charge cost separately.

facts.label: Accessibility
facts.value: Developed visitor facilities include the exhibit hall and tower complex, but individual trails, elevator service, docks, and wet outdoor surfaces vary. Contact the center before traveling for a specific accommodation.

facts.label: What hours is Anne Kolb Nature Center open?
facts.value: The Broward County exhibit-hall page currently lists nature centers and their exhibit halls open daily from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Tower, trail, gate, event, and paddling access can close separately for weather, maintenance, or programming, so call 954-357-5161 before a time-sensitive visit.

facts.label: What address should I use for Anne Kolb Nature Center?
facts.value: Use 751 Sheridan Street, Hollywood, FL 33019. The entrance is on the north side of Sheridan Street east of Federal Highway. Navigate to the nature center, not a generic West Lake shoreline point, because most of the preserve is mangrove wetland without road access.

facts.label: Where should I park at Anne Kolb Nature Center?
facts.value: Use the on-site visitor parking reached from the Sheridan Street entrance. Park once for the exhibit hall, tower, and nearby short trails; the separate West Lake Park marina and South Trail approaches should not be assumed to use the same lot.

facts.label: Is Anne Kolb Nature Center free?
facts.value: The current Broward County exhibit-hall page says there is no admission fee to the nature centers or exhibit halls. Programs, rentals, meeting spaces, events, and any posted weekend or holiday gate fee can cost separately; confirm before a rental-dependent visit.

facts.label: Are there restrooms at Anne Kolb Nature Center?
facts.value: Restrooms and visitor services are available at the developed nature-center complex during building hours. Use them before heading onto the tower, fishing-pier route, or longer outdoor paths because facilities are not distributed throughout the mangrove preserve.

facts.label: Is Anne Kolb Nature Center accessible?
facts.value: The developed visitor complex includes indoor exhibits and a five-level observation tower, but elevator operation, trail surfaces, docks, and weather exposure can affect access. Contact the center at 954-357-5161 before travel for a specific mobility, sensory, or program accommodation.

facts.label: Are dogs allowed at Anne Kolb Nature Center?
facts.value: Do not plan on bringing a pet into this wildlife-focused mangrove preserve. Service-animal access and a specific accommodation should be confirmed with Broward County Parks before visiting indoor exhibits, narrow boardwalks, or wildlife-sensitive areas.

facts.label: What can children do at Anne Kolb Nature Center?
facts.value: The free exhibit hall has interactive mangrove displays, a hands-on Eco-Room, and a short theater video. Families can add the observation tower and a short trail, but should bring water, insect repellent, sun protection, and close supervision around stairs, railings, docks, fishing areas, and tidal water.

facts.label: What trails are at Anne Kolb Nature Center?
facts.value: The visitor complex connects to short nature routes and fishing access through a mangrove environment, while the broader preserve also includes longer gravel and paddling routes. Surfaces can be wet, exposed, or uneven; get the current trail map at the visitor center and ask which routes are open.

facts.label: What are the main landmarks at Anne Kolb Nature Center?
facts.value: The signature landmarks are the five-level, 68-foot observation tower, the exhibit hall and Eco-Room, the mangrove boardwalks and nature trails, the Intracoastal fishing pier, the outdoor amphitheater, and views across the 1,501-acre wetland.

facts.label: Can I kayak at Anne Kolb Nature Center?
facts.value: The West Lake and Anne Kolb complex includes designated non-motorized paddling routes through mangrove wetland. Rental availability, launch location, route conditions, and last-return times can change, so confirm with the center or marina before bringing or renting a boat.

facts.label: Can I reach Anne Kolb Nature Center by transit?
facts.value: Yes. Broward County Transit identifies Anne Kolb Nature Center as a destination. Plan the current route to 751 Sheridan Street and check the last return trip before entering a trail or program because published route numbers can change.

facts.label: What weather should I plan for at Anne Kolb Nature Center?
facts.value: The tower, boardwalks, fishing areas, and trails are exposed to South Florida heat, lightning, heavy rain, mosquitoes, and slick surfaces. Leave the tower and water at the first sign of thunder, carry drinking water, and check the forecast before choosing a long outdoor route.

facts.label: What wildlife might I see at Anne Kolb Nature Center?
facts.value: The protected mangrove wetland supports native and migratory birds plus aquatic wildlife. Observe quietly from developed routes, never feed or approach animals, keep hands away from water and mangrove edges, and use insect protection without disturbing habitat.

facts.label: What should I know before visiting Anne Kolb Nature Center?
facts.value: Start in the exhibit hall for the current map and closure status, then choose one destination rather than assuming the 1,501-acre preserve is a single walkable loop. Confirm tower elevator and paddling availability, use restrooms first, and carry water, sun and insect protection, and a lightning exit plan.

facts.label: Anne Kolb Observation Tower
facts.value: The five-level, 68-foot Anne Kolb Observation Tower rises above the mangrove estuary and provides broad views toward West Lake, the Intracoastal Waterway, and the Atlantic coast.

places.name: Hollywood North Beach Park

facts.label: Cost and fees
facts.value: There is no ordinary gate admission, but the county charges a parking fee instead. Current rates can change and park passes do not cover this parking charge.

facts.label: Accessibility
facts.value: The developed park includes an ADA-compliant boardwalk ramp and recent accessible gangway improvements. Sand, tides, weather, individual piers, and construction can still affect a specific route, so confirm critical access before travel.

facts.label: Address

facts.label: What hours is Hollywood North Beach Park open?
facts.value: Broward County's current park listing does not publish a dependable daily gate schedule, so confirm park and parking hours before a time-sensitive visit. Hollywood Ocean Rescue currently staffs the municipal beach from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. year-round and until 7:00 p.m. on holidays and special events. Broward County parks are closed December 25.

facts.label: What address should I use for Hollywood North Beach Park?
facts.value: Use 3601 N Ocean Drive, Hollywood, FL 33019 for the county park. Decide whether you want the Atlantic beach side or the Intracoastal picnic and fishing side before parking; North Ocean Drive separates visitor experiences within this long coastal park.

facts.label: Where should I park at Hollywood North Beach Park?
facts.value: Use the county-operated park parking and choose a space near the side you plan to visit. Parking is the primary access charge and is not included with a Broward Parks Passport. Rates and special-event pricing can change, so read the current fee schedule and posted pay-station instructions before leaving the car.

facts.label: Is Hollywood North Beach Park free?
facts.value: General entry is not normally charged at a gate, but parking is paid. The Broward Parks Passport page specifically says the pass does not cover Hollywood North Beach Park parking. Recheck the current county fee schedule because daily, afternoon, holiday, and oversized-vehicle rates can change.

facts.label: Are there restrooms at Hollywood North Beach Park?
facts.value: Yes. Broward County planning records identify restrooms among the facilities distributed through the park's five pocket-park areas. Use the nearest open restroom before settling on the beach or fishing because facilities are spread along a long shoreline and can close for maintenance.

facts.label: Is Hollywood North Beach Park accessible?
facts.value: The park includes an ADA-compliant boardwalk ramp to the beach and Broward County has documented accessible gangway and service improvements. Sand, weather, tides, pier approaches, and construction still vary, so contact the park before travel for a specific mobility or transfer need.

facts.label: Are dogs allowed at Hollywood North Beach Park?
facts.value: Do not bring a pet onto the Hollywood North Beach Park beach side. Broward County excludes that beach side from its general leashed-dog allowance, and the City of Hollywood directs beachgoing dogs to the separate designated Dog Beach between Pershing and Custer streets. Service-animal rules remain separate.

facts.label: Are there lifeguards at Hollywood North Beach Park?
facts.value: Hollywood Ocean Rescue provides year-round beach lifeguard service across the city beach system, currently 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. and until 7:00 p.m. on holidays and special events. Not every stretch should be assumed staffed at every moment; check flags, choose a visible staffed tower, and keep children and weak swimmers within direct reach.

facts.label: Can I fish at Hollywood North Beach Park?
facts.value: Broward County permits fishing from the park's Intracoastal piers and shoreline. Use the Intracoastal side rather than a swimming area, keep hooks and lines away from other visitors and wildlife, and check current Florida saltwater-license rules and posted restrictions before fishing.

facts.label: Can I picnic at Hollywood North Beach Park?
facts.value: Yes. Official sources identify picnic areas and shelters in the park. Choose the Atlantic or Intracoastal side first, confirm reservation requirements for a shelter or group, secure food from birds and wind, and remove everything before leaving.

facts.label: Is there food at Hollywood North Beach Park?
facts.value: Visit Lauderdale lists a café among the park's visitor facilities, but concession hours and availability can change independently from beach access. Bring drinking water and verify current service before relying on the café for a meal, especially early, late, or during severe weather.

facts.label: Can I reach Hollywood North Beach Park by bus?
facts.value: Yes. Broward County Transit Route 4 identifies Hollywood North Beach Park as a served destination. Check the current Route 4 schedule, stop direction, and last return trip before leaving because beach time can extend past convenient service.

facts.label: What should I know about sea turtles at Hollywood North Beach Park?
facts.value: Sea-turtle nesting season runs March 1 through October 31. Never touch a turtle or nest, avoid flash photography and bright lights at night, remove chairs and belongings, fill holes before leaving, and report an injured or stranded turtle through the city's posted contacts.

facts.label: What weather should I plan for at Hollywood North Beach Park?
facts.value: The beach, piers, tower, and picnic areas are exposed to heat, sun, wind, lightning, heavy rain, rough surf, and changing currents. Check the forecast and beach flags, carry water and sun protection, leave piers and water when thunder is heard, and do not enter the ocean on prohibited flag conditions.

facts.label: What should I know before visiting Hollywood North Beach Park?
facts.value: Choose Atlantic beach access or the Intracoastal fishing and picnic side before parking, expect a parking charge, check beach flags and lifeguard hours, use a restroom before settling in, and remember dogs are not allowed on this beach side. During turtle season, remove gear, fill holes, and avoid flash or bright nighttime lighting.

facts.label: Are restrooms and showers available at Mizell-Johnson State Park?

facts.label: What accessible facilities are at Mizell-Johnson State Park?
facts.value: Accessible amenities include beach boardwalks, parking, picnic facilities, restrooms, marina facilities, and Whiskey Creek Hideout. Beach wheelchairs are available first-come, first-served from the entrance station; call ahead for a critical accommodation.

facts.label: Are dogs allowed at Mizell-Johnson State Park?
facts.value: Pets are welcome only in designated areas on a hand-held leash no longer than six feet. They are not allowed on beaches or natural shorelines and may not be left unattended. Service animals are allowed under Florida State Parks policy.

facts.label: Are there lifeguards at Mizell-Johnson State Park?
facts.value: No lifeguards are on duty. Swimming is at your own risk. Read the warning flags, stay out on double-red conditions, never swim near the jetty or boat traffic, and keep children and weak swimmers within direct reach.

facts.label: Where can I kayak at Mizell-Johnson State Park?
facts.value: Whiskey Creek is a 1.5-mile mangrove-lined paddling route. The official concession rents canoes, kayaks, and paddleboards. Check tides, wind, lightning, rental cutoff, and return time; wear a fitted PFD and stay alert for boats outside sheltered water.

facts.label: Is there food at Mizell-Johnson State Park?
facts.value: Yes. Whiskey Creek Hideout is the official concession and offers a restaurant, limited picnic supplies, ice, and watercraft and beach rentals. Hours and inventory can change, so bring drinking water and confirm before relying on it for a meal.

facts.label: What trails are at Mizell-Johnson State Park?
facts.value: The park lists a 0.4-mile Barrier Nature Trail through coastal hammock, a three-mile service-road route, and more than two miles of beach walking. Expect heat, sand, roots, insects, standing water, and limited shade; do not enter posted closures.

facts.label: Can I reserve a pavilion at Mizell-Johnson State Park?

facts.label: Can I launch a boat at Mizell-Johnson State Park?

facts.label: What is currently closed at Mizell-Johnson State Park?

facts.value: Regular park hours are 9 a.m. to sunset, with sunset times posted at each area entrance. Fishing, boat launching, and permitted hunting can use different authorized hours; confirm those activities with the park rather than assuming the day-use gate schedule applies.

facts.value: Current day-use charges from April through October are $2 per vehicle for Maryland residents and $4 for nonresidents on weekdays, then $3 per person for residents and $5 per person for nonresidents on weekends and holidays.
